title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 99
paragraphs: Aristagoras meanwhile, when the Athenians had arrived with twenty ships, bringing also five triremes of the Eretrians (who joined the expedition not for the sake of the Athenians but of the Milesians themselves, to repay a debt they owed—for the Milesians in former times had borne with the Eretrians the whole burden of that war which they had fought with the Chalcidians, when the Chalcidians on their side were helped by the Samians against the Eretrians and Milesians)—when these, I say, had arrived and the other allies were on the spot, Aristagoras proceeded to march on Sardis. On this march he did not go himself, but remained at Miletus and appointed others to command the Milesians, namely his brother Charopinus and a certain Hermophantus from among the other citizens.
